title: Hybrid chunked embedding import orchestrator with idempotent job API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid chunked embedding ingestion orchestrator that supports both streaming uploads and large bulk manifests via an idempotent async job API. The goal is to handle very large corpus imports (millions of documents) with bounded memory, predictable latency for small requests, and clear semantics for retries and deduplication using idempotency keys. This ticket covers API surface, orchestration, worker-side chunk checkpointing, failure modes, metrics, and rollout gating.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/embeddings/import starts an async job and returns a stable job_id when an Idempotency-Key header is provided; repeated requests with the same key return the same job_id and do not re-ingest already-completed items.

Support two transport modes: (A) chunked streaming uploads (chunk size configurable up to 8MB) that can resume from last committed chunk via job checkpoints; (B) manifest-driven bulk import where client uploads objects to S3/GCS and provides a manifest URL.
Per-item processing status is exposed via GET /v1/embeddings/import/{job_id}?detail=true including success/failure reason and model variant used.

At-least-once processing is default; when client supplies an idempotency-key and per-item client_id, the orchestrator guarantees effectively-at-most-once ingestion for matching client_id within the lifespan of the job (de-dup table retention window documented).

System gracefully handles partial-worker failures: in-flight chunks are retried by orchestrator with exponential backoff and jitter; job-level failure states include failed, partial, and completed with per-item error counts.
Autoscaling targets: a sustained import of 100k items/min should keep median per-item enqueue latency under 200ms and median end-to-end embedding latency under 800ms for small items (<=512 tokens).

Observability: job-level metrics (items_total, items_processed, items_failed), per-model latency histograms, idempotency key hit rate, and retention of job audit logs for 90 days available in Console.
implementation_notes: API: Add POST /v1/embeddings/import with optional Idempotency-Key header. Body accepts mode: 'stream' or 'manifest'. For stream mode, server returns upload_url and job_id and accepts chunked POST to /v1/embeddings/import/{job_id}/chunks with chunk_index and checksum headers.

Job orchestration: Use existing job-queue service (Kafka-backed) with a lightweight coordinator service that records job metadata and chunk checkpoints in the primary metadata DB. Checkpoints recorded per-chunk include committed_offset, checksum, and worker_id.

Deduplication: Maintain a write-optimized dedup table keyed by (idempotency_key, client_item_id) with TTL configurable per-customer (default 30 days). Writes are conditional so that repeated ingestion attempts for the same idempotency_key are no-ops.

Chunking & resume: Clients may upload up to N chunks per job concurrently. Coordinator returns last_committed_chunk on resume; worker validates chunk checksum before processing and acknowledges commit to coordinator for durability.

Backpressure: Implement token-bucket queueing at the coordinator; when queue depth exceeds threshold, new streaming uploads receive 429 with Retry-After and a push-back hint header to reduce client concurrency.

Batching heuristics: Workers aggregate small items up to a model-dependent token threshold (configurable per model-profile) to maximize GPU utilization while respecting per-item latency SLOs. Use dynamic batching window (20-80ms) and size caps derived from model profile.

Failure semantics: Per-item errors (e.g., unsupported encoding) mark item as failed and are checkpointed; transient worker errors trigger retry with exponential backoff and jitter. System exposes per-item retry_count.
Storage: Temporary chunk storage uses Tiered object store (local fast SSD then S3). Chunks flushed to durable store only after commit. Manifest mode only stores pointers to client-provided URIs.
Security: Validate Idempotency-Key scope to the customer account and enforce checksum verification for all chunks. Include KMS-wrapped metadata for on-prem customers when required.
Observability: Emit job lifecycle events to tracing system and create aggregate metrics for job throughput and item success rate; wire up Console dashboard for beta customers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for coordinator: idempotency-key semantics, checkpoint updates, conditional writes to dedup table.
Integration tests: simulated chunked upload with resume scenarios across coordinator restart, worker crash during processing, and repeated POSTs with same idempotency key.
Load test: synthetic dataset of 10M items via manifest mode to validate autoscaling and ensure 99th percentile per-item enqueue latency stays below SLA.
Correctness: Compare embeddings produced by async import path to synchronous /v1/embeddings for a representative corpus to detect quantization/regression issues.
Chaos & durability: kill worker processes mid-job and validate orchestration properly retries and does not double-ingest on idempotent replays.
Security tests: fuzz Idempotency-Key header parsing, chunk checksum mismatches, and unauthorized manifest URL access attempts.
Beta customer verification: run two pilot customers through their real ingestion pipeline and collect key metrics and feedback before ramping to general availability.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated behind org-level opt-in. Enable only for internal accounts initially.
Beta release to 3 existing customers with varying dataset shapes (short docs, long docs, mixed). Monitor idempotency-key collision rate and per-item failure reasons for two weeks.
Progressive ramp: move from 3 customers -> 15 customers -> 100 customers over 6 weeks if health signals (errors, latency, cost) are within thresholds.
GA after 90 days of stable beta metrics and completed security review. Document migration guide for customers using older ingest endpoints.
Provide automatic fallback: when coordinator detects sustained worker OOMs for a model, it will fallback to a lower-throughput but high-reliability ingest path and surface debug link in Console.
